question: Under Ontario Regulation 129/04, what credential must an operator hold to work as an operator at a Class 2 wastewater treatment facility?
correctAnswer: A valid wastewater treatment operator certificate of the class required for the facility
explanation: Regulation 129/04 requires operators of wastewater facilities to hold a valid operator certificate of the appropriate type and class for the facility where they work. Experience or an owner's permission does not replace certification.

A general contractor licence issued by the municipality
A university degree in environmental science
A letter from the facility owner stating the operator is experienced

question: Wastewater arriving through a long force main smells strongly of rotten eggs at the headworks. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: Anaerobic conditions during the long travel time allowed sulfate reducing bacteria to generate sulfide
explanation: Long detention in a full force main turns the wastewater septic, and sulfate reducing bacteria produce sulfide. Released at the headworks, it gives the rotten egg odour of hydrogen sulfide.
options: The wastewater was too cold when it entered the sewer
The force main is made of the wrong colour of pipe
Anaerobic conditions during the long travel time allowed sulfate reducing bacteria to generate sulfide
Excess chlorine was added at the pumping station
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide
